The superalloy PWA-1480 has a nominal composition of Ni-12Ta-10.4Cr-5Co-5Al-4W-1.5Ti (wt%).
Single crystal PWA-1480 specimens with [001] growth direction within ±8° were used in the experiments.
The thermal gradient (G1) in the melt at the tip of the primary dendrite array was approximately 140-150 K cm^-1 at the liquidus temperature of 1610 K.

The primary dendrite spacings initially decreased along the length of the solidifying samples before becoming almost constant, indicating steady-state solidification conditions were achieved after about 1 cm of growth.
The secondary arm coarsening kinetics did not show any appreciable difference between the high gravity and low gravity periods.
The microsegregation profiles for elements like Ta, Al, and Ti showed the same trends in both the high and low gravity regions.
The estimated solute diffusivity in the PWA-1480 melt was in the range of 0.8 to 3.4 x 10^-5 cm^2/s.

The time required to reach a certain fraction of the final steady-state fluid velocities after a change in gravity is much shorter (about 2 seconds) than the duration of the low gravity periods in the KC-135 flights (18 seconds).
The initial side branch spacing near the tips of the primary dendrites scales linearly with the tip radius, which is determined by the solutal profile in the melt at the dendrite tips.
Unlike carbon-containing superalloys, PWA-1480 does not have carbide precipitate formation, making it a good model system to study the effects of gravity on solidification behavior.
The final solidification of PWA-1480 at the base of the primary dendrite array occurs at nearly a constant temperature, similar to the isothermal eutectic solidification in a binary system.

The growth speed was assumed to be the same as the furnace withdrawal speed, and the distances from the quenched primary dendrite tips were correlated with the various high and low gravity periods of the flight.
Typical cooling rates of approximately 50 K/s were recorded during quenching by the thermocouple located near the tips of primary dendrites.
The portions of the mushy zone that solidified during high-g and low-g periods were marked in the longitudinal microstructures of the samples.
The scatter in the composition data was minimal near the tips of primary dendrites, but quite large (10-20%) in the quenched interdendritic liquid region.
